choices_help.help: Create the bare clone + seed state.
Full-tree indexing (resumable).
Content-based staleness check: paths whose chunks predate their last change at the branch head; --heal re-ingests them (watermark untouched).
OPTIMIZE ... FINAL a code vector table when its physical copies per key reach --min-ratio, and wait for the merge. Dry run by default (measures the ratio); --apply optimizes.
Write the namespace's live chunks under a second embedding model's label: in-database, resumable, no checkout.
Fill a namespace's Matryoshka-prefix twin of the chunk vectors inside ClickHouse: no re-embed, resumable.
SQL/shell test -> implementing C++ reference pass (writes code_test_map method=content_reference; idempotent).
Import the newest per-test line coverage run of the configured source (writes code_test_map method=coverage and code_coverage_files).
Export (query -> acted-on unit, hard negatives) retrieval pairs from real traffic (trace x outcome join) for embedder/reranker fine-tuning.
Merged-PR history from GitHub.
Regenerate context packs for recently merged PRs in the current pack shape.
LLM contextual one-liners for top-PageRank chunks.

Tombstone cached code.ask answers (after a synthesis-model upgrade, stale weaker-model answers would otherwise be served forever — the cache only self-invalidates on cited-file change). Dry run by default (counts and samples the matches); --apply tombstones.

Full compiler-tier re-index by hand (the code_scip_full worker runs it weekly by default: heals the TU-cap degrades of per-merge deltas and any drift). Heavy: ~50 min of scip-clang + apply, on this host rather than in the server.

Print the entry's compiler-tier lock file on this host. A manual harness run goes under `loom code entry-lock`, which takes this file and the deployment lease; scip-full and scip-delta take both themselves.
Run a command under the entry's compiler-tier lock (this host's file and the deployment's lease): exit 75 when another pass holds it, 3 when the lease is lost mid-run (the command is stopped).
One compiler-tier delta pass (same code as the code_scip_delta worker), by hand: git_head vs scip_commit per configured repo, scip-clang over the changed TUs, apply. Prints `RESULT: ...`.
One line per configured repository: org namespace checkout lock-file (the lock path resolved; a manual run takes it through `loom code entry-lock`).

Pre-seed the code.ask answer cache from a question list (one question per line, or JSONL with a 'question' field). Each miss pays one synthesis; every future asker fleet-wide gets the cached answer. Safe to re-run: hits are free.
Reset a failed SCIP batch to pending.
Inline review comments for merged PRs already in code_pr_history that have none stored yet (newest first, one GitHub request per PR).
Fill code_pr_history.assignees (who the repo assigned to review) for merged PRs already stored, walking the newest closed PRs 100 per request.
Fill code_gh_items (issues + PRs, any state) updated since a date, 100 per request, oldest update first; moves gh_items_cursor.
Watermarks + live row counts.
Maintenance matrix from merged-PR co-change: 'when this file changes, these usually change too', with evidence, as markdown for an instructions file (AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md).
Agent-instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions, .claude/**.md, skills) whose path or symbol references no longer resolve at the clone's head.

choices_help.help: Mine one knowledge document into decision records: the model reads the document whole (or in windows of whole sections past LOOM_MEMORY_DECISION_EXTRACT_WINDOW_CHARS; a heading over only an image and its caption is not sent), again when its reply holds no decision, and writes each decision's outcome, reasons and rejected options in its own words, each claim citing quotes of the text. A claim none of whose quotes is in the text is left out, and a decision whose outcome quote is missing or only in a recap, summary or background section is dropped; a second call, the support check, keeps only the claims their quotes state and reads the extractor's stored rows against the text. Kept decisions are written through decision.record as agent loom-decisions. A re-run revises or retires the extractor's own rows the text no longer states and tags a pinned or attested row source-changed instead: pinning or attesting freezes a row against re-extraction. Dry run by default (still calls the model); --apply writes. Exits 1 when it could not run on the document (no document, no chunks, no usable model, model calls held for the org, which stops the run with nothing more written and nothing retired, an unknown --repo or a namespace it may not use, --into without --repo or source on another repository's namespace, a --repo with no remote to tag rows with, the dashboard's repositories unread, its own rows unreadable, left in another namespace or linked to another repository, no window read), 2 when a write, or a read it needed (a window or its support check included), was refused or failed (a row changed since the run read it is reported, not counted).

Leaves a manual knowledge_source_sync row in loom.worker_status. Exits 1 when a source's turn or a document's extraction failed.

Move document originals held in ClickHouse to LOOM_DOCUMENT_S3_BUCKET: each one whose catalog row still holds its bytes is written to its own object with the store's SHA-256 check, read back and hash-verified, and its row then names the object, so every document with those bytes downloads from the bucket. The ClickHouse copy stays until loom.document_blobs merges its parts (OPTIMIZE TABLE loom.document_blobs FINAL drops it now). Needs LOOM_DOCUMENT_OBJECT_STORE=s3, set on every replica first so no new original lands in ClickHouse behind the walk. An original an unfinished erasure covers (its namespace or an uploader) is not moved; a move an erasure overtakes is taken back, or named to run that erasure again. Idempotent: run it again to go on after a stop. Exits 1 when an original was not moved (bytes that do not hash to their sha256 or fill their size, an erasure not yet finished, a bucket that refused); it stays where it was.

ch-setup.description:
`loom ch-setup`: prepare a ClickHouse that Loom did not start itself, a
self-managed server or a ClickHouse Cloud service, for Loom's first boot.

It creates the `loom` database and the read-only reader user
(`LOOM_CH_READER_USER`, default `loom_reader`): SELECT on `loom.*` and a
settings profile that pins Loom's caller-shaped caps as ceilings, with floors
no statement can go under. Run it again at any time: what is in place is left
alone, and a reader whose profile or grants differ from that is rebuilt to
exactly it, so changes an admin made to the reader do not survive a rerun.

A user without the privilege for a step gets the SQL to hand an admin instead,
with the password left as a placeholder. The bundled ClickHouse defines the
reader in its config, so there it only reports. An existing reader is
replaced only when it has the shape ch-setup gives it (a password user on the
settings profile of its own name) and logs in with LOOM_CH_PASSWORD; anything
else of that name is left alone.

choices_help.help: Code intelligence plane operations.
Decision records mined from documents.
Knowledge documents and their sources.
Render a namespace as an OKF v0.2 bundle (Markdown + frontmatter) — the git-reviewable projection of Loom memory.
Write the concepts of an OKF v0.2 bundle into a namespace via memory.set.
Lint an OKF bundle directory offline — the compile gate a mirror repository's CI runs. Exit 2 critical, 1 warnings, 0 clean.

Boot the local stack (Loom, its document extractor and ClickHouse) and print how to connect: creates .env and the ClickHouse config from their templates, runs docker compose up --build, waits for /v1/health, then prints the dashboard URL and the first memory.set (curl + Python SDK) and `claude mcp add` snippets — minting a writer token first when auth is on. Re-run any time.
Stop the local stack while preserving data; --delete-data performs a confirmed reset.
Prepare a self-managed ClickHouse or a ClickHouse Cloud service for Loom: create the loom database and the read-only reader user, or print the SQL for an admin.
The Loom processes a provider change waits for.
The configuration every replica checks itself against.
Every setting's value in force, and overrides of the live ones.
Credentials and signing keys stored sealed in ClickHouse.
The token signing keys beside LOOM_JWT_SECRET, kept in ClickHouse.
The provider configuration lock.
Write one UTC day of usage and a namespace snapshot to S3 as Parquet, names hashed under LOOM_ANALYTICS_EXPORT_NAME_KEY. Never replaces an object, so a repeated run is safe.

Re-embed vectors whose embedding_model != the configured embedder (run after changing LOOM_EMBEDDING_MODEL — Loom does not auto-re-embed). Covers memory, entity, and conversation vectors. Coded vector tables keep their width: change a model of another width in Settings → Models & keys, which rebuilds them.

Replay a namespace's raw evidence (memory.set_from_messages turns) through a running server's write path into ANOTHER namespace — the current extractor over the stored transcripts; the source is never written.

What a colour swap changed: the deployment's ledger rows (volume, errors, p50/p95, upstream spend per operation) and its ClickHouse statement shapes (runs, bytes, seconds) for a window on each side of the swap, with flags for what moved past a coarse threshold.

Export a namespace's entity graph (co-occurrence edges + triples) to GraphML or JSON-LD for an external graph or RDF tool. Read-only; every edge carries its provenance and a note that a path is declared, not proven.

How a namespace is being used (namespace.audit): exact-key reads vs searches, hash keys, double-encoded and oversized values, hand-rolled index rows, leases stored as memories, version churn. Read-only; prints a table (code, severity, kind, count, share, first sample) or --json. Exit 1 on a critical finding.

The store's advice to one agent (mentor.brief): what it called, the planes its namespace offers, the hints with their evidence, and how often past hints were followed. Read-only; prints a table or --json. Exit 1 when a warning-level hint fires.
Boot the control plane (uvicorn).
Apply schema migrations against the configured CH.

Re-emit memory_embeddings rows whose status diverged from loom.memory (superseded / conflicted / duplicate marks the pool never saw), compared and re-emitted per identity row (org, namespace, agent, user_id, session_id, key). Dry run by default (counts by status, the rows it would write); --apply writes.
Write period digests — one derived episodic memory over K consecutive session digests of each identity in one namespace. Additive and idempotent. Dry run by default (plans only); --apply writes.

Find a namespace's extracted facts that narrate tool activity ('User read lines 1-1000 of X', 'Claude ran a command on …') with no durable outcome and demote (confidence x0.25) or label them through memory.apply. Dry run by default; keys an agent read by name in the last --days are left alone. Never deletes.
Re-probe the embedder + run per-NS calibration immediately (otherwise this runs weekly via the recalibration worker).

Import a ClickGap (Detector→Validator→Reviewer) SQLite export into Loom (lessons + typed entities + categories). Reembed-only; preserves kind→memory_type, per-row TTL, recall_count (→ ranking via reinforcement_count), suppression polarity, and provenance. Idempotent via deterministic keys + per-run version.

Import an external vector-recall agent-memory SQLite export into Loom. Introspects the DB at runtime (schema not assumed): tables are classified by column heuristics into memories (→ memory.set) or conversation transcripts (→ conversation.append, grouped by conversation id); unmatched tables/rows are skipped, never crash. Idempotent via deterministic keys.

Import a markdown agent 'brain' directory into Loom: MEMORY.md (always-injected HOT layer) → profile.set sections; memory/contexts/*.md (read-on-demand WARM layer) → knowledge.add docs. Completes the migration alongside import-recall (the deep vector layer). Missing files are skipped, never crash.
Release a self-signup claim: revoke its grants, clear the owner, deactivate it. The name stays reserved.
Mint a JWT locally (requires LOOM_JWT_SECRET).
Revoke one token by jti or subject (writes loom.revoked_tokens through the revocation module; needs the configured ClickHouse).
Carry password accounts over to single sign-on.
Bots and CI jobs that sign in with a key or their CI's identity.

Diagnose pre-boot misconfig (Python version, settings, JWT, CH reachability) and print the problem list /v1/health carries, each with its fix. With --client, also examine this machine as a coding-agent client.
Print the bug form's Environment field: versions and the `loom doctor` checks.
Print the memory ingest drop ledger (loom.memory_drops) for a namespace, by stage/reason — what the pipeline discarded, truncated or gave up on.

List (default) or erase throwaway namespaces — finished bench runs under the bench prefixes that nobody registered and nobody has written to for --idle-hours — in one list-scoped erasure saga per batch.

Re-verify failed erasure sagas: print each one's last step-named reason and a fresh residue census (default, read-only); --resume re-runs them from their checkpoint past the recovery worker's attempts budget; --orphan-graph lists namespaces whose entity graph outlived their memories and, with --erase, purges them.
Read-only first contact with the tracker source: counts and newest timestamps per upstream table per credential, breaker states, the configured tracker namespaces.

Read-only: does each tracker source's schema meet the record contract (docs/features/tracker/record-contract.md)? Names missing tables / columns, optional tables present, feature columns. Exit 0 when every checked source meets it.
Refit tracker.duplicate_check's calibrated confidence for one tracker namespace now: replays the duplicate gold at filing time, fits, stores the fit.

Clear the tracker_embed pass cursors of one tracker namespace so the next pass re-walks the window and re-embeds every item whose text recipe changed. Dry run by default (prints the cursors); --apply clears them.
Give namespaces that hold live memory and no registry row an owner row: kind=bench under the bench prefixes, else memory; retention_days 0, no TTL. Dry run unless --apply.

Label live rows the sensitivity detector would have labelled on write but a path skipped. Dry run by default: counts by level, probe shape and namespace. --apply writes one new version per row, tombstones a high row's embedding rows and tags a medium row's. The closing line is the high-sensitivity invariant (high rows with a live embedding).

Read the row-level integrity gauges (dim-0 rows holding a vector, tombstoned_at/status drift, active rows past valid_to) and, with --apply, re-emit the dim-0 rows with their true dimension so search can return them again. Drift and valid_to are listed, not repaired.

Re-chunk and re-embed a namespace's knowledge documents from stored content through the current chunker, so every document carries section metadata, chunk context and document frequency. Idempotent; one embedding per new chunk. Dry run by default (counts the documents and chunks); --apply re-chunks.
Export the action schema derived from the operation registry — an MCP tools/list manifest with loom extras (json) or the Cedar schema (cedar) a policy gateway governs the surface with.
Recompute BM25 document frequency for a namespace from its live rows (the term-frequency views only see inserts; supersession and tombstones leave stale vocabulary behind).
Print installed Loom version.

Wire Loom into a local AI client's config. Writes the MCP server block into Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code's config file, atomically, merging with anything already there; for Claude Code it runs (or prints) `claude mcp add` and for Codex `codex mcp add`. Restart the client afterwards.

The first five minutes: ingest this repo's AGENTS.md (or --file) into the knowledge plane the way `make ingest` does, ask it a question, and print the answer with its evidence rows. On the stock fake-LLM stack it prints the top knowledge.search hits and says what a real answer needs.

Create an identity on a Loom server. `--agent NAME` signs an agent up by itself (server needs LOOM_SELF_SIGNUP=open): mints a writer token on a fresh agent-<slug> namespace, saves it to ~/.loom/token, and prints the one-time code a person uses in the dashboard to claim the namespace.

Pipe a chat-history file (markdown / JSON) into Loom's conversation table as one thread. Generic ingest for tools without an MCP integration (Aider, Continue.dev, JetBrains AI, anything else): export the chat → run this command → the thread shows in the dashboard's Conversations.
Run a memory.search from the shell. Default human output; --json-agent emits a structured envelope agents can pipe through (a `{command, results}` JSON shape).

Designate the Loom host(s) for this deployment. Writes the given login handle(s) or email(s) to LOOM_PLATFORM_ADMINS in the .env (--env-file, default ./.env): a handle promotes that password account to platform_admin, an email promotes an SSO sign-in with that verified email. Multiple OK (on-call rotation, co-operators, etc.). Re-login required after to pick up the role.
Sign in to a Loom server on any browser with a one-time code.
End the stored session on the server and forget it here.
Show who the stored session signs you in as.
Call any operation or API route with the stored session (`loom call --help`).
Make, list and revoke your own tokens for CI and agents (`loom token --help`).
